This is the start of the episode (1.6-6.4 s). The arm moves steadily from its start pose to the toaster: the wrist view goes from a distant view of the toaster to a close view of its front and top, with the bread standing in the left slot. In the shoulder views both toaster levers are still at the top of their tracks at 6.4 s, so the lever has not been pushed yet. This is normal approach motion.

The gripper is at the front-left of the toaster next to the left lever; the wrist camera shows the lever stem just below/in front of the fingers (closest at 11.2 s). The bread still sticks up out of its slot at the same height in all four frames and the visible lever sits at the top of its slot, so the lever has not been pushed down yet. The robot is in the middle of approaching the lever, which is normal progress this early in the episode.

At 14.4-16.0 s the gripper is at the toaster front on the left lever (the side with the bread). In the wrist view at 16.0 s the lever block sits low on its track, consistent with having been pushed down. At 17.6-19.2 s the arm rises above the toaster, and the wrist view shows the bread standing in its slot just beyond the open fingers, which looks like the approach for the bread. The left lever itself is hidden by the gripper in both shoulder views, so the lever state is not fully confirmed. The bread has not been picked yet.

The bread slice stands up out of the left toaster slot in every frame (popped up, not lowered for toasting), so the lever stage appears finished. The gripper is above the toaster at the bread the whole time: the wrist view shows the bread getting closer to the finger tips (20.8 -> 24.0 s) and the camera turning around it (25.6 s). At 25.6 s the bread is still in the slot and has not been lifted. It is unclear whether the fingers have closed on it; if this hovering continues it would be no_progress, so confidence is low.

answer.event_detail: Toaster: the empty gripper hovers over the top of the toaster, above the right slot next to the bread, for the whole 4.8 s without pressing a lever or grasping the bread.
answer.evidence: Zooming on the toaster front, both levers sit at the top of their slots (up) in all four frames, and the bread sticks up out of the left slot at the same height throughout. The gripper stays above the toaster's right half; the wrist camera only sees the toaster's top grill and holds nothing. The plate stays empty. From these frames I cannot tell whether the lever was pushed earlier and has already popped up (that would make stage 1 done); with the lever up and no sign of toasting I mark stage 1 as not done.

The bread slice stands up out of the left toaster slot in all frames, so the toaster is not toasting now. At 33.6-35.2 s the gripper is above the toaster slots (wrist view looks into the grills, with the bread at the edge). At 36.8-38.4 s it moves down to the toaster front: the wrist view shows a lever block at the top end of its track, very close to the fingers. That looks like the start of pushing the lever. I cannot tell whether the lever was already cycled earlier (bread popped) or never pushed. Nothing is grasped and the bread has not been moved.

answer.event_detail: The gripper circles the toaster for the whole 40.0-44.8 s window. It hovers in front of the right-hand lever (the one for the empty slots), never pressing it, then moves over the top to the bread at 44.8 s without grasping it.
answer.evidence: Wrist views at 40.0-43.2 s show the toaster front close up, with both lever blocks at the slot end of their tracks (not pushed down). In the shoulder views both levers stay up and the bread stays standing in the left slot in every frame. At 44.8 s the bread is just beyond the closed finger tips but has not been taken. I cannot see whether the lever was cycled earlier in the episode, so stage 1 is marked not done with low certainty.

answer.event_detail: Toaster/bread: the empty gripper hovers just to the right of the bread slice sticking out of the toaster for 4.8 s, without closing on the bread or pressing a lever.
answer.evidence: Left shoulder view: the arm pose barely changes across the four frames, gripper beside the bread above the toaster's right half. Zoomed toaster front: the left lever sits at the top of its slot and the bread stands fully up out of the slot in every frame. Wrist camera: the bread slice is in view above the fingers, not between them, shifting only slightly. The plate is empty. I cannot tell from these frames whether the toaster was already run and popped up (which would make stage 1 done); with the lever up and no sign of toasting I mark stage 1 as not done, low confidence.

answer.event_detail: Bread slice in the toaster: the gripper comes down onto the bread (52.8-54.4 s) with fingers closed together beside it, then pulls back and moves away (56.0-57.6 s) while the bread stays standing in the toaster slot.
answer.evidence: Wrist camera at 52.8/54.4 s shows the bread right at the closed finger tips; at 56.0 s and 57.6 s the bread is farther away, still in the slot, and nothing is between the fingers. Both shoulder views at 57.6 s show the bread still sticking up from the left slot of the toaster and the arm pulled back. Stage 1 is judged done because the bread is up out of the slot and the robot has moved on to the bread, but I cannot see the lever cycle in this clip. Both toaster levers are at the top of their tracks, so the toaster is not running now. That fits a finished toast cycle, but an unpushed lever looks the same.

answer.event_detail: The gripper hovers in the air to the right of and above the toaster for the whole 4.8 s (59.2-64.0 s), fingers closed and empty, drifting slightly away. It touches neither the lever nor the bread.
answer.evidence: Both shoulder views show the arm in nearly the same raised pose next to the toaster in all 4 frames. The bread stays standing in the left slot. The wrist view shows the toaster and bread receding, with nothing between the fingers. Stage 1 cannot be confirmed: the bread is up, which fits either a lever never pushed or a toast that already popped, and no lever motion is visible in this clip.

The kettle stays on the counter to the right of the stove in all four frames; a pot sits on the stove. The arm moves from above the pot (1.6 s) to above the kettle (3.2 s) and descends with open fingers (4.8-6.4 s). At 6.4 s the wrist camera shows the open fingers straddling the kettle's top handle, close to it, but the kettle has not been lifted. This is a normal approach to grasp; no burner is lit.

The kettle is held by its top handle the whole time (the wrist camera shows the handle between the fingers in every frame). It is carried from the right side over to the stove (8.0-9.6 s) and is positioned over the large left burner at 11.2 s and 12.8 s. At 12.8 s the gripper still holds the kettle and it seems to hover slightly above the burner cap (the burner ring is visible under it), with no release seen. So the placement is not finished yet. The arm barely moves between 11.2 and 12.8 s, which may just be the slow final descent. No burner is lit. Ambiguity: the kettle is at or just above the target burner, so stage 1 is almost done, but it has not been released.

At 14.4-16.0 s the gripper holds the kettle over the left burner area. By 17.6 s it has let go: the kettle stands upright on the left burner's grate and the arm moves away. The wrist camera shows the kettle sitting slightly toward the back of the left burner, overlapping the rear of the burner cap rather than centred on it, but clearly on the stove. At 19.2 s the arm moves toward the front of the cooktop and the wrist camera faces the control knobs; no burner shows a flame or glow, so the left burner is not on yet. The robot is making normal progress on stage 2. Small doubt: the kettle is off-centre on the burner.

The kettle stands upright on the large left burner of the cooktop in every frame and is not in the gripper. From 20.8 to 24.0 s the gripper is at the front-left control knob (the wrist camera centres on that knob, and its indicator line rotates between frames). At 25.6 s a blue flame ring shows on the left burner, directly under the kettle, in both shoulder views. So the left burner is on with the kettle on it, and the task looks complete.

In every frame (27.2-32.0 s) the kettle stands upright on the large left burner, with a blue flame ring visible under it in the left shoulder view. So the kettle is on the stove and the left burner is lit, and both stages are done. At 27.2 s the gripper is just leaving the front-left knob. Afterwards (28.8-32.0 s) the arm swings right toward the pot on the right side of the stove, which is motion after the task is complete; the kettle and the flame are not affected.

In all four frames the kettle stands upright on the large left burner, with a blue flame ring under it (left and right shoulder views). So the kettle is on the stove and the left burner is on, and both stages are done. Meanwhile the arm works on the pot on the right side of the stove: from 33.6 s to 38.4 s it pushes or drags the pot forward, and the pot is visibly tilted by 36.8-38.4 s. This is extra motion after completion that disturbs an unrelated object but does not undo either stage. If this post-completion interference counts as a failure, it would be 'other' (pot tilted by the arm).

answer.event_detail: After the task is done, the robot picks up the pot (not a task object) and carries it onto the left burner, pressing it against the kettle that is already sitting there; the kettle gets pushed or rotated.
answer.evidence: At 40.0 s the kettle stands upright on the large left burner with a blue flame under it, and the gripper is at the pot on the right side of the stove. At 41.6-43.2 s the pot is lifted and carried left (right shoulder view; the wrist camera shows the pot rim filling the view and the kettle on the blue flame just beyond it). At 44.8 s the pot is right against the kettle on the left burner. In the left shoulder view the kettle's handle, edge-on at 43.2 s, now shows as a loop, so the kettle has been rotated or tilted by the contact. At 44.8 s the kettle still appears to be on the left burner and blue flame is still visible under it, so both stages still hold, but the extra pot motion risks knocking the kettle off. Uncertain how far the kettle has moved, because the arm partly hides it.

answer.event_detail: The robot has set the pot (not a task object) down on the left burner, crowding the kettle that was already there and pushing it toward the back of the burner; it then goes back to the left burner knob.
answer.evidence: At 46.4 s the pot sits on the left burner area, pressed against the kettle; the kettle is upright behind it, and a blue flame shows at the left edge of the burner. From 48.0 to 51.2 s the arm leaves the pot and moves to the front-left knob. At 48.0 s the wrist camera shows the knob indicator in a turned position, and at 49.6-51.2 s the gripper is right over that knob. At 51.2 s the kettle is still upright on the cooktop at the back of the left burner, behind the pot, and blue flame is still visible at the left of the burner. So both stages appear to hold, but the kettle is no longer clearly centred on the burner, and the robot is handling the knob again, which could switch the burner off. Ambiguous: the pot and arm hide most of the burner, so how much of the kettle is still over the flame is uncertain.

In every frame the pot sits on the large left burner, with the kettle standing upright right behind it at the back of the left burner grate. Blue flame is visible at the left edge of that burner throughout (left shoulder view; wrist camera at 54.4-57.6 s). So the kettle is on the stove and the left burner is lit. Neither the kettle nor the pot is held; the arm only moves around the front-left of the cooktop (52.8 s at the left knob, then lifting and turning away), with no new change to the scene. Caveat: the pot, not the kettle, occupies the centre of the lit burner, and the kettle is crowded toward the back, so whether the kettle still counts as on the burner is somewhat uncertain.

In all four frames the pot sits on the large left burner, with the kettle upright directly behind it at the back of the left burner grate. A blue flame is visible at the left edge of that burner in every frame, including 64.0 s (left shoulder view; wrist camera at 59.2-62.4 s). So the kettle is on the stove and the left burner is lit. Neither object is held. From 59.2 to 62.4 s the arm hovers almost motionless at the front-left of the cooktop; at 64.0 s it lowers toward the control knobs again (the wrist camera shows the knobs, with the left knob in a turned position). This is idle motion after the task is done. Caveat: the pot occupies the centre of the lit burner and the kettle is pushed toward the back, so whether the kettle still counts as on the burner is somewhat uncertain; and if the arm now turns the left knob, the burner could go off.

answer.event_detail: Kettle: the open gripper comes down right over the kettle at 4.8 s (over the lid, handle not between the fingers), then at 6.4 s it is high above the counter with the fingers closed and the kettle still standing on the counter.

answer.event_detail: Kettle on the counter right of the stove: the open gripper hovers above it, descends (9.6 s), rises again (11.2 s) and descends again (12.8 s) without grasping.

answer.event_detail: Kettle: the gripper moves around above the kettle on the counter with its fingers closed on nothing, comes somewhat closer at 24.0 s, then drifts back over the right side of the stove at 25.6 s without grasping it.

answer.event_detail: Kettle still on the counter right of the stove at 27-32 s. The empty gripper moves over the stove and pan (27.2 s), lifts up (28.8-30.4 s) and swings back high above the kettle (32.0 s) without picking it.

answer.event_detail: Kettle: the gripper, fingers closed on nothing, hovers above the kettle on the counter to the right of the stove for 4.8 s without descending to grasp it; at 44.8 s it drifts left away from the kettle.

answer.event_detail: Kettle: the gripper, with its fingers already closed on nothing, hovers above the kettle on the counter next to the stove for the whole 4.8 s, moving up and back down without grasping or lifting it.

answer.event_detail: Kettle on the counter right of the stove: 60 s into the episode the gripper is still hovering above it. It moves closer (60.8 s), backs off (62.4 s) and comes close again (64.0 s) without grasping, with the fingers nearly closed and not around the handle.

Start of the episode (1.6-6.4 s). The drawer under the counter is already pulled out, with the knife lying inside. The knife is not yet grasped and the cutting board is empty. This is normal approach motion.

The gripper is down inside the open wooden drawer; the wrist camera shows the knife lying in the drawer, and by 12.8 s the gripper is centered and aligned above the knife handle, ready to grasp.
